note: Barre chords from either root string: major, minor and 7 on one root with the root on the low E string, then on the A string, one chord in both places on a caged-neck, then a four-chord song with no open chords on a strum-along. The old Key choice is now moves (any key): the first two blocks pin their key, since which string the lowest barre shape takes its root from changes with the key, and the caged-neck gives the key the rest moves from, and the song's chords are tokens counted the long way once. missing: chord-shapes with "voicing": "barre" draws the 7 as a four-string shape and not the full barre 7, and takes no root string, so one chord can't be shown on both roots (caged-neck does it, for a major chord only).

exercise.title: Any chord, two places
exercise.why: A movable shape has its root under finger 1, on the low E string or on the A string, so the note under that finger names the chord and every chord can be played in two places.

cells.heading: Root on the low E string

cells.text:
Below are three barre chords on one root: major, minor and 7. Press a chord box below to hear it. Fret the three in turn: the root stays under finger 1 on the low E string for all of them.
Pick the strings of each chord one at a time, and fix only the one that buzzes.

Below are major, minor and 7 on a new root. Press a chord box below to hear it. Fret the three in turn: now the root is under finger 1 on the A string, and the low E string stays out of the strum.
Practice until you can go round the three without looking at the chord boxes.

The neck below shows one major chord twice: the shape with the root on the low E string, and the shape with the root on the A string, further up the neck. Strum it in the first place, then in the second.
Then move both shapes to new roots: find the root on the low E string or the A string first, and put finger 1 on it.
_Stop and shake out your hand when it aches._

The song has four chords. {{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}. {{chord:vi}} is the 6th chord, built on {{6}}. {{chord:IV}} is the 4th chord, built on {{4}}. {{chord:V7}} is the 5th chord with a 7th, built on {{5}}.
Press a chord box below to see its barre shape. Then press Play under them to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}, and strum the chord in the lit box.
If a change comes late, keep your strumming hand going and catch the next beat 1.
{{?key}}In another key the roots move along the two strings, and a chord may take its other shape where that one sits lower.
